rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS)
rules.description: Matching HTML tags using regular expressions is hard to do right, and can easily lead to security issues.
An array index is compared to be less than or equal to the 'length' property, and then used in an indexing operation that could be out of bounds.
User input should not be used in regular expressions without first being escaped, otherwise a malicious user may be able to inject an expression that could require exponential time on certain inputs.
The 'else' clause of an 'if' statement should be aligned with the 'if' it belongs to.

rules.cwe_name: Reliance on Undefined, Unspecified, or Implementation-Defined Behavior
rules.description: If the id of an HTML attribute is malformed, its interpretation may be browser-dependent.
Using indexOf to implement endsWith functionality is error-prone if the -1 case is not explicitly handled.

rules.cwe_name: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
rules.description: Comparing different kinds of HTTP request data may be a symptom of an insufficient security check.
The operand of the 'delete' operator should always be a property accessor.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
rules.description: Using regular expressions to expand self-closing HTML tags may lead to cross-site scripting vulnerabilities.
A restricted route, URL, script, or file can be requested directly without required authorization.
